summary: The Patients Deserve Price Tags Act amends the Public Health Service Act, Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to strengthen health care price and coverage transparency requirements. The bill establishes new disclosure mandates for hospitals, clinical diagnostic laboratories, imaging service providers, ambulatory surgical centers, and health plans, requiring them to publicly post standard charges, negotiated rates, and ownership information in machine-readable formats. It also introduces requirements for itemized billing, advanced explanations of benefits, patient hold-harmless protections against excessive bills, and enhanced federal oversight of administrative service providers.

affected_groups.effect: Must publicly disclose standard charges, cash prices, and ownership details quarterly, comply with standardized reporting formats, submit senior official attestations, and face potential civil monetary penalties and collection restrictions for noncompliance.
affected_groups.group: Hospitals, clinical laboratories, imaging service providers, and ambulatory surgical centers

affected_groups.effect: Must provide enrollees with real-time self-service cost-estimation tools, publish machine-readable rate and payment files quarterly, submit compliance attestations, and ensure contracts with service providers do not restrict data access.
affected_groups.group: Health plans, health insurance issuers, and group health plan sponsors

affected_groups.effect: Receive expanded access to pricing data, itemized bills, advance explanations of benefits, and hold-harmless protections against bills that substantially exceed good faith estimates.
affected_groups.group: Patients, beneficiaries, and health care consumers

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new transparency rules prohibiting gag clauses, requiring quarterly data disclosures to group health plans, and imposing daily civil penalties of up to $100,000 for violations.
affected_groups.group: Administrative service providers, third-party administrators, and pharmacy benefit managers

key_provisions: Requires hospitals, clinical laboratories, imaging service providers, and ambulatory surgical centers to compile and publish standard charges, gross charges, discounted cash prices, and payer-specific negotiated rates on a quarterly basis in a machine-readable format.

Mandates that health plans and health insurance issuers provide enrollees with comprehensive self-service tools and disclosures regarding in-network rates, out-of-network amounts, and cost-sharing liabilities.

Prohibits health care providers from taking extraordinary collection actions against patients if the hospital was noncompliant with price transparency rules or if billed amounts substantially exceed good faith estimates without documented medical necessity.

Requires health care providers to include written notices of the right to request an itemized bill, containing plain-language descriptions, billing codes, and prices, within 30 days of receiving final payment.
Prohibits agreements between group health plans and administrative service providers that restrict or delay plan access to claims, encounter data, and pricing methodologies.
Establishes civil monetary penalties for noncompliance with transparency, reporting, and data-sharing rules, including daily fines for providers, laboratories, surgical centers, and health plans.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for civil monetary penalties where the statutory text leaves the specific amount to be specified by the Secretary through rulemaking.
The precise criteria and definitions the Secretary will establish for certain medical terms, exemptions, and lookback windows.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Patients Deserve Price Tags Act amends the Public Health Service Act, Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to strengthen health care price and coverage transparency requirements. The bill establishes new disclosure mandates for hospitals, clinical diagnostic laboratories, imaging service providers, ambulatory surgical centers, and health plans, requiring them to publicly post standard charges, negotiated rates, and ownership information in machine-readable formats. It also introduces requirements for itemized billing, advanced explanations of benefits, patient hold-harmless protections against excessive bills, and enhanced federal oversight of administrative service providers.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping update to federal health care transparency laws, significantly expanding public price disclosure requirements across multiple types of medical facilities and insurance plans. By enforcing strict data-sharing mandates, limiting collection actions on noncompliant entities, and imposing substantial financial penalties for violations, the legislation aims to give consumers and plan sponsors greater visibility into medical pricing and administrative costs.
